Gemariah
gem-uh-RYE-uh
proper noun
Hebrew Gemaryah (H1587), the LORD has accomplished or the LORD has completed — from gamar (H1584), to end, to complete, to perfect, and Yah, the covenant name.

Biblical Definition

Gemariah the son of Shaphan the scribe was one of the princes of Judah in Jehoiakim's reign, and he behaved well in a court that did not. It was his chamber in the higher court of the LORD's house that Baruch used to read Jeremiah's roll in the ears of all the people (Jer 36:10). His son Michaiah heard the reading and carried word of it down to the princes in the scribe's chamber (Jer 36:11-12). And when the roll had been brought to Jehoiakim and the king began cutting it up leaf by leaf and feeding it to the hearth, three men tried to stop him: Nevertheless Elnathan and Delaiah and Gemariah had made intercession to the king that he would not burn the roll: but he would not hear them (Jer 36:25). They failed. A second Gemariah, son of Hilkiah, was one of the two envoys Zedekiah sent to Babylon who carried Jeremiah's letter to the exiles (Jer 29:3). The house of Shaphan runs through the whole period as the family that kept sheltering the prophets, and Gemariah is one of its better members.

Origin & Era

A prince of Judah under Jehoiakim, son of Shaphan the scribe, in whose chamber Baruch read Jeremiah's roll and who pleaded with the king not to burn it.

GEMARIAH, Hebrew Gemaryah, the LORD has accomplished.

1. Son of Shaphan the scribe, a prince of Judah in the reign of Jehoiakim.

Baruch read the words of Jeremiah in his chamber in the house of the LORD.

He was one of three who made intercession that the king would not burn the roll.

2. Son of Hilkiah, sent by Zedekiah to Babylon, who carried Jeremiah's letter to the captives.

Key Scripture

Jer 36:10 — "Then read Baruch in the book the words of Jeremiah in the house of the LORD, in the chamber of Gemariah the son of Shaphan the scribe, in the higher court, at the entry of the new gate of the LORD'S house, in the ears of all the people."

Jer 36:11 — "When Michaiah the son of Gemariah, the son of Shaphan, had heard out of the book all the words of the LORD,"

Jer 36:12 — "Then he went down into the king's house, into the scribe's chamber: and, lo, all the princes sat there, even Elishama the scribe, and Delaiah the son of Shemaiah, and Elnathan the son of Achbor, and Gemariah the son of Shaphan, and Zedekiah the son of Hananiah, and all the princes."

Jer 36:25 — "Nevertheless Elnathan and Delaiah and Gemariah had made intercession to the king that he would not burn the roll: but he would not hear them."

Modern Corruption

Faithfulness is measured by whether it succeeded; Gemariah pleaded, was refused, and is named in Scripture for the pleading.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. Gemariah is uncontested. The pressure he applies is on our way of scoring obedience. Three princes stood up in a royal chamber and asked the king not to burn the word of God. The king burned it anyway, and then sent to arrest Baruch and Jeremiah. By every outcome-based measure the intercession accomplished nothing: the roll went into the fire leaf by leaf while they watched.

The Holy Ghost saw fit to record their names anyway, and to record them as the men who tried. That is how Scripture usually scores things. It is required in stewards, that a man be found faithful (1Co 4:2) — faithful, not successful. Noah preached a hundred and twenty years and saved eight people. Jeremiah preached forty and saw the city burn. And the roll itself outlived the fire: God simply told Jeremiah to take another roll and write all the former words, and there were added besides unto them many like words (Jer 36:32). The principle to recover is that the obligation is to speak, and the outcome belongs to God, who is perfectly capable of replacing what a king can burn.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Gemaryah (H1587), from gamar (H1584), to complete, to accomplish, with Yah.

expand to see more

Hebrew gamar (H1584) — to end, complete, accomplish; the LORD will perfect that which concerneth me (Psa 138:8).

Hebrew Gemaryah (H1587) — son of Shaphan (Jer 36:10-25) and son of Hilkiah (Jer 29:3).

Hebrew Shaphan (H8227) — Shaphan the scribe, who read the book of the law to Josiah; head of a house that sheltered prophets.

Hebrew megillah (H4039) — a roll, a scroll; the roll Jehoiakim burned.

Hebrew paga (H6293) — to make intercession, to entreat; what the three princes did before the king.

Usage

"“Elnathan and Delaiah and Gemariah had made intercession to the king”."

"“But he would not hear them”."
